targetTest: denies the line, and one approval of the request named spends nothing: the line is denied again and a second request is named
expected: with one approval, git push origin main; git push origin main is denied again and the lone approval stays unspent
actual: with the repeated command counted once (planted in the working tree), the single approval covered both commands and the line was allowed
semanticAssessment: PLANTED CHANGE: in consumeLine of src/hook/pre-tool-use.ts the commands were de-duplicated by action and parameter digest, so a repeated command needed one approval, applied in the working tree only and reverted after the run. The correct implementation of Task 1 already counts a repeated command twice, so the repeated-command test passed against it (unexpected green); the planted change is the defect the test exists to catch. Against it the target test ran to its own assertion and failed on 'one approval let a line run a command twice' (outcome allow, expected deny); the older-approval test failed too, as a consequence (its setup needs the second approval that the planted change never asks for), and the other tests of the file passed (51 of 53). Not a load, fixture or parse fault.
